finalText:
`async` and `defer` only change how an external classic script (`<script src>`) is fetched and run. Module scripts have their own defaults, and for inline classic scripts both attributes do nothing.

**Plain script (the baseline).** With neither attribute, the script is fetched and evaluated immediately, and parsing stops until both are done. The spec says so: "If neither attribute is present, then the script is fetched and evaluated immediately, blocking parsing until these are both complete." (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html)

**`async` (external classic script).**
- **Parsing:** the script is fetched in parallel with parsing. It is evaluated as soon as it has arrived, "potentially before parsing completes". The parser therefore pauses only while the script runs, not while it downloads.
- **DOMContentLoaded:** there is no fixed relationship. The script can run before or after the event. MDN says `DOMContentLoaded` "doesn't wait for other things like images, subframes, and async scripts to finish loading". MDN also says the event fires "before the execution of scripts with async" in its readyState note, which is a typical case rather than a guarantee. (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event)
- **Order:** none. In the spec's processing model, async scripts go into a *set* of scripts that will execute as soon as possible, not a list. Each one runs when its own fetch finishes, so a later script in the markup can run first. (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html)

**`defer` (external classic script).**
- **Parsing:** the script is fetched in parallel with parsing but evaluated only "when the page has finished parsing".
- **DOMContentLoaded:** deferred scripts run after parsing finishes and before `DOMContentLoaded`. MDN states that "Scripts with the defer attribute will prevent the DOMContentLoaded event from firing until the script has loaded and finished evaluating." During their execution `document.readyState` is "interactive". (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event)
- **Order:** deferred scripts run in document order. The spec appends each one to the document's "list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing", and MDN states the in-order guarantee. This holds even if a later script downloads first. (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script)

**Both attributes together.** MDN says that if both are present the element acts as if only `async` were specified. The spec says `defer` may be added alongside `async` so that legacy browsers that support only `defer` fall back to deferring rather than blocking. (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html)

**Inline classic scripts.** MDN warns that `async` and `defer` must not be used without `src`, and that for classic scripts they would have no effect. An inline classic script runs immediately and blocks the parser. This follows from the spec's algorithm. The async, defer and in-order branches apply only to a classic script with a `src`, or to a module. Any other classic script runs immediately, "even if other scripts are already executing", or is held while the parser waits on a style sheet that blocks scripts. (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html)

**`type="module"` scripts.**
- **`defer`:** a module script is deferred by default. The spec says: "(The defer attribute has no effect on module scripts.)". MDN says "they defer by default". Module scripts also join the same list as `defer` scripts, so they run in document order, after parsing and before `DOMContentLoaded`. MDN's `DOMContentLoaded` page lists `<script type="module">` among the deferred scripts the event waits for. (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event)
- **`async`:** with `async`, the module and all its dependencies are fetched in parallel and evaluated as soon as they are available, like async classic scripts. Order is no longer guaranteed.
- **Inline modules:** these are deferred too, because the spec's `defer`-or-module branch has no `src` condition. With `async`, an inline module runs as soon as it is ready. Even then it does not run synchronously, because the spec queues a task before marking it ready.

**Dynamically inserted scripts.** The spec's algorithm also covers scripts created by JavaScript rather than by the parser:
- **`force async`:** these scripts get a "force async" flag, and the `async` getter then returns true. Unless you set `async = false`, they behave as async.
- **`async = false`:** a dynamic script that is not async goes into the "list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible". These run in insertion order but not after parsing. (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html)

**Summary.**

| Case | Blocks parser while fetching? | Runs | Order guaranteed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain | Yes | Immediately | Yes |
| `async` | No | When ready | No |
| `defer` | No | After parsing, before `DOMContentLoaded` | Yes |
| Module | No | Like `defer` | Yes |
| Module + `async` | No | When ready | No |

I found no conflicts between the sources, which are the WHATWG spec and MDN. Two edges are worth knowing. MDN's wording that `DOMContentLoaded` fires "before the execution of scripts with async" describes the typical case, not a rule. The spec itself gives no ordering between `async` scripts and that event.
